text:
janet: Quick micro-sync on Dedicated release: we still need final wording for incident credits, the canary fail/fallback lexicon, and what we commit in docs vs contract. Can we resolve before next legal review?

miguel: From infra perf tests: with autoscale steady we hit p95 ~180ms, p99 ~420ms on baseline configs. For strict SLAs I recommend p99=500ms and a burst headroom policy rather than a static buffer. That lets us keep costs down but be predictable.

priya: For docs + SDKs, we need a clear developer contract: what falls under "compatible fallback" and when features (e.g., function-calling, long KV cache) may be unavailable. Prefer explicit per-route opt-in for auto-fallback.

janet: Agree on opt-in. Customers should opt-in per-model or per-route to allow non-preserving fallbacks. We can have a default "preserve semantics" mode that blocks fallback unless enabled.

miguel: Implementation note: default preserve mode will failover only to variants that support the same APIs. If user permits relaxed semantics, fallback can go to quantized variants that may have trimmed long-context support.

priya: I'll add a snippet to QuickStart showing how to enable relaxed fallback in SDKs.


sara: Legal comments: credits need to be simple. We can't keep complex stepwise tables in contract. Suggest one-line formula and a cross-reference to the SLA doc for examples. Also call out maintenance carve-outs.

janet: Can we agree on a short credit formula that legal likes and FinOps can model? Something linear but capped.

tom: Proposal: credit = min(30%, floor(total_downtime_minutes / 30) * 5%). So every 30m -> +5% up to 30% cap. Maintenance with 72h notice = no credit. Scheduled window used for upgrades that affect >10% customers flagged in billing.

tom: In code form:

```
credit_pct = min(30, floor(downtime_minutes / 30) * 5)
```

miguel: I prefer an approach that also distinguishes partial-impact incidents (e.g., single-region, subset of tenants). We can include a weighting factor for affected capacity: effective_credit = credit_pct * affected_share. But legal may hate fractional math.

sara: Legal: fractional credits are ok if we define measurement methods precisely (how "affected_share" is computed). Keep the formula short and reference an annex.

aisha: Monitoring/alerting: we should separate "contract SLO" (what triggers credits) from internal "operational SLO" (what oncall cares about). Suggest contract credit trigger = sustained p99 > SLA for 10 minutes OR error-rate > 1% for 5 minutes. Internal alerts should fire earlier.

aisha: Canary policy proposal:

```
canary_pause_if: (error_rate > 0.5% for 3m) OR (p99 > SLA_threshold for 5m)
on_fail: rollback + route to fallback variant + create incident ticket
```

janet: Good. We should also require automatic telemetry flagging so customers can reconcile requests routed to fallback (billing & logs).

miguel: We'll add a header in responses when fallback occurred: X-Redwood-Fallback: true and route_variant: <id>. Also add telemetry metric fallback.count_by_route.

priya: Docs: add a section "When fallback occurs" that includes sample SDK response handling and a small client example to retry or force fallthrough.

tom: Pricing nuance: credits reduce overage charges only, not committed reservation fees. If customer consumes below commitment, credits apply to next invoice line item. Need to be explicit.

sara: I'll draft contract text: short paragraph plus cross-ref to SLA.md as annex. Avoid long examples in the contract itself.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy initiated by miguel at 1768234710  8/16 nodes  monitoring p95/p99 per-shard.

miguel: Canary update: minute 12, one shard showed p99=610ms, canary paused automatically, we rolled that shard back and rerouted traffic. Flagged fallback for 3 requests. No customer-visible errors.

janet: That's a good real example we can mention in docs (anonymized) as a runbook case.

priya: I'll draft a runbook snippet: immediate commands, who to page, how to force rollback, and a postmortem template.

janet: Action list: 
- miguel: confirm SLA numbers (p95/p99) + headroom auto-scale policy by Wed EOD (1768320910).
- aisha: finalize canary triggers and alert mapping, add to PagerDuty by Wed.
- tom: produce the simple credit formula and a billing note for contracts by Thu.
- sara: draft contract paragraph and annex reference by Thu EOD.
- priya: update docs and SDK examples with fallback header and opt-in snippet by Fri.

janet: If we get these done we can land the SLA annex into the Dedicated contract and ship the docs with GA. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

miguel: Ack. I'll also add a telemetry dimension for "opt_in_relaxed_fallback" to measure adoption.

sara: I'll loop in revenue ops to ensure billing math is tested before legal sign-off.

janet: Perfect. Close unless blockers. :v:
